purpose: Track EUROMOD-platform issues and workarounds that affect current household-level Axiom oracle comparisons. Issues tied only to retired non-documentary Belgium surfaces are archived with those reports.

entries.summary: Running Belgium BE_2025 under the bundled BE_training_data dataset name can abort during preparation because some income lists are registered only under real SILC dataset-name conditions while formulas that reference them still compile.

workaround.description: Run the policy system under the real dataset configuration name while templating synthetic rows from the bundled training-data schema. This reads no licensed SILC records.

entries.summary: The Belgium BE_2025 employer social-contribution policy tscer_be appears to use stale Fonds de fermeture des entreprises company-closing-fund rates: 0.06 percent and 0.12 percent, while the official ONSS 2025 workbook gives 0.18 percent and 0.23 percent including wage moderation for commercial employers below and above the 20-worker threshold. In the ordinary less-than-20-worker synthetic cases, EUROMOD returns exactly 26.75 percent of post-uprating yem while the source-backed RuleSpec path returns 26.868876 percent.

workaround.description: Keep the residual visible in the household-level oracle report and do not alter RuleSpec away from official ONSS 2025 DmfA instructions and the 2025 FFE workbook while the upstream EUROMOD issue is open.

entries.summary: Static XML inspection suggested the Belgium BE_2025 self-employed social-contribution policy tscse_be might use a 19.65 percent main-activity first-bracket rate while the current consolidated upstream Royal Decree No. 38 Article 12 text in corpus states 20.50 percent. The 2026-07-03 live household oracle did not reproduce that discrepancy: after EUROMOD uprated yse to 31,650.67 EUR, EUROMOD tscse_s and Axiom both returned 6,488.39 EUR, exactly the statutory 20.50 percent path.

observed_with.function: SchedCalc: SIC self-employed: main activity before retirement age and not receiving pension

workaround.description: No live workaround required for the main-activity household slice. Keep the statutory RuleSpec rate at 20.50 percent and keep this ledger entry as a superseded static-inspection note unless a future live case reproduces a real rate residual.

entries.summary: The Belgium BE_2025 self-employed social-contribution policy tscse_be treats Royal Decree No. 38 Article 12 section 2 and Article 13 section 1 thresholds as deductible allowances in secondary-activity and post-pension cases. The source text makes them eligibility/exemption thresholds: below the threshold no contribution is due, but once reached, contributions apply to the stated professional-income bands rather than to income net of the threshold.

cases.note: EUROMOD applies the 96.44 EUR quarterly low limit even though yse is below the indexed Article 12 section 2 threshold.
EUROMOD subtracts the indexed Article 12 section 2 threshold before applying the 20.50 percent rate.
EUROMOD subtracts the indexed Article 13 section 1 threshold before applying the 14.70 percent rate.

statutory_evidence.statutory_article_12_section_2: No contribution is due below 405.60 EUR base; when income reaches at least that amount, annual contributions are 20.50 percent and 14.16 percent on the stated professional-income bands.
statutory_evidence.statutory_article_13_section_1: No contribution is due below 811.20 EUR base; when income reaches at least that amount, annual contributions are 14.70 percent and 14.16 percent on the stated professional-income bands.

workaround.description: Keep the secondary and post-pension residuals visible in the household-level oracle report and do not adjust the RuleSpec away from Royal Decree No. 38 while the upstream EUROMOD issue is open.

entries.summary: The Belgium BE_2025 special social-security contribution policy tsceesp_be differs from Law of 30 March 1994 Article 108: single-household thresholds/cap behavior are mistyped, and the joint-assessment schedule appears to put a zero-rate band where Article 108 requires the 1.3 percent band, then starts 1.3 percent in the statutory plateau band.

observed_with.base_bridge: EUROMOD il_taxabley returned by the engine is bridged into RuleSpec Article 107 household income

cases.note: EUROMOD exceeds the statutory 731.28 EUR single-household maximum contribution.
EUROMOD does not apply the statutory joint 1.3 percent band above 21070.96 EUR.
Same joint schedule issue in the mid joint band.
EUROMOD starts the 1.3 percent band in the statutory plateau range rather than applying the 632.39 EUR plateau.

statutory_evidence.statutory_joint_middle_band: 123.95 EUR plus 1.3 percent of household income above 21070.96 EUR from 21070.97 EUR through 60181.95 EUR

workaround.description: Keep the affected high-income single and joint-assessment residuals visible in the household-level oracle report and do not alter the RuleSpec statutory schedule while the upstream EUROMOD issue is open.

entries.summary: The Belgium BE_2025 Flemish jobbonus policy bwkrg_be appears to use older thresholds, a 600 EUR maximum, a 20 EUR full-time small-payment threshold, and no 2025 fixed top-up, while the Flemish Government implementing order consolidated as of 1 January 2025 sets 2,115/3,114.99 EUR thresholds, a 650 EUR maximum, a 50 EUR floor/full-time small-payment threshold, a 10 EUR part-time small-payment threshold, and a 50 EUR fixed top-up when payable. The expanded live suite also shows the 10 EUR part-time suppression case matches at zero.

workaround.description: Keep the residual visible in the household-level oracle report and do not alter RuleSpec away from the Flemish Codex and 2025 implementing order while the upstream EUROMOD issue is open.

entries.summary: The Belgium BE_2025 immovable-withholding policy tprhm_be computes khooo_s as the raw cadastral-income product khooo * 2.2446, while CIR 92 Article 518 requires rounding the indexed cadastral income to the nearest euro.

statutory_evidence.article_518_rule: Index cadastral income by the annual coefficient and round to the nearest euro.

workaround.description: Keep the rounding residual visible in the household-level oracle report and do not remove the CIR 92 Article 518 rounding rule from Axiom while the upstream EUROMOD issue is open.

entries.summary: UKMOD's Universal Credit output bsauc_s embeds a benefit take-up correction: the DEF policies BTA_uk and random_uk seed a per-benefit-unit take-up draw (i_rand_tu) that bsauc_uk gates the award on (for example the condition i_bsauc_grptu = 3 & (i_rand_tu#1 <= $ISTUNoChild)). For a hypothetical household the draw can mark the benefit unit as a non-taker and return a zero award that is not the statutory entitlement. The take-up draw is a STOCHASTIC per-row modelling device for representative-population take-up calibration, NOT a per-household deterministic rule, so it does not identify a reproducible statutory result for a hypothetical benefit unit. Corrected 2026-07-05 (batch-size-1 integrity audit): the earlier claim that the zeroing is deterministic per composition/earnings with neighbours returning the full award was WRONG. Verified live on UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03 (system UK_2026, dataset training_data) by running byte-for-byte identical households: ten identical copies of the entitled couple-owner household in one run return [666.97, 666.97, 0.0, 666.97, 666.97, 0.0, 0.0, 666.97, 666.97, 666.97] and ten identical single-owner-no-capital households return [424.90, 424.90, 0.0, 424.90, 424.90, 0.0, 0.0, 424.90, 424.90, 424.90] — identical facts, different awards purely by row position, so the zeroed set is a draw, not a function of earnings or composition. Where the unit takes up, bsauc_s equals the Axiom statutory entitlement exactly (single 424.90, couple 666.97), so the Axiom encoding is correct and the zeros are a UKMOD-side stochastic artefact. Which cases zero is not reproducible: the committed dashboard report records one realization (all 19 cases in one batch = 11 mismatches); re-running at batch size 1 gives 8 mismatches, with three take-up zeros resolving (couple-owner, couple-2child-owner, single-owner-capital0) and two persisting purely by draw (earn15000, earn30000), while the deterministic benefit-cap, NIC-rounding, and capital-boundary mismatches are byte-identical across both batchings.

attempted_switches.BTA_uk_off: No effect: the adapter policy-switch override sets the BTA_uk policy off, but the take-up draw is initialised in InitVars_uk (always on) and gated inside bsauc_uk, so the award still zeros.
attempted_switches.random_uk_off: No effect for the same reason.
attempted_switches.TUDef_uk_off: Breaks the run: TUDef_uk defines the benefit assessment units, so UC cannot be computed without it.
attempted_switches.per_case_isolation: Does NOT stabilise the result (corrected 2026-07-05). Running each case alone (idhh=1, --comparison-batch-size 1) does not remove the take-up draw and does not resolve to a stable earnings/composition pattern: three of the five all-in-one-batch take-up zeros resolve to the full award at batch size 1 while two persist, and running identical households one-per-batch still yields different awards, because the draw is stochastic per row rather than a reproducible per-household rule. Batch size 1 is therefore not a fix for this instrument; the only per-household-deterministic UKMOD configuration would force 100% take-up (disable the i_rand_tu gate), which the exposed policy switches (BTA_uk, random_uk) do not achieve. Update (per-household adapter isolation, 2026-07-06): the worker now runs every household as its own engine run, so each case reproducibly gets its solo draw sequence — WHICH cases zero is now stable across runs, batch sizes, and batch compositions (no more realization-by-batch). This stabilises the recorded realization; it does not recover the statutory entitlement for cases whose solo draw marks non-take. Forcing 100% take-up now has a working mechanism: the adapter's euromod_constant_overrides patches DefConst values (e.g. the take-up rates) into the system XML on the model overlay — the connector's constantsToOverwrite kwarg silently ignores DefConst constants. Adopting it for this suite is a deliberate regeneration (values flip from take-up realizations to statutory entitlements), tracked for the suite owner.

workaround.description: Compare the composed rulespec-uk UC award against the executed bsauc_s and classify take-up-driven zeroing as a UKMOD-side stochastic artefact, not an Axiom encoding mismatch. Because the take-up draw is not reproducible per household, the committed dashboard report is one realization: it records the take-up zeros produced by running the whole suite in a single batch, dispositioned by pinned value. The comparison is monthly-to-monthly (bsauc_s is left un-annualized). Where a unit takes up, the composition and capital families return clean statutory entitlements that match the Axiom award to the penny (verified monthly: single 424.90, couple 666.97, single+1child+rent 1526.78, and a capital tariff of 4.35 per 250 above 6000); the take-up-zeroed points are dispositioned rather than absorbed by tolerance. A future adapter fix that forces 100% take-up (see the batch-position adapter-fix task) would make this suite deterministic and let the take-up zeros be dropped; batch size 1 alone does not (three of five zeros resolve, two persist by draw).

entries.summary: UKMOD does not apply the regulation 80A/81 benefit cap to Universal Credit for hypothetical benefit units in UK_2026: the award rises one-for-one with rent with no plateau (verified across a rent sweep for a couple with two children: 500/month rent -> 1774.85, 1000 -> 2274.85, ..., 3000 -> 4274.85). The composed rulespec-uk pipeline applies the cap (22,020/year outside Greater London = 1,835/month), so awards above the cap diverge by exactly the UKMOD uncapped award less the cap. UKMOD ships a benefit-cap policy (bcap_uk) but it does not bind for these synthetic households (the cap has an earnings/grace-period exemption path).

workaround.description: Classify awards above the regulation 80A cap as an upstream UKMOD benefit-cap gap in dispositions/uk-universal-credit.yaml, with the arithmetic reconciling the UKMOD uncapped maximum against the capped Axiom award. Below-cap cases match to the penny.

entries.summary: At exactly 16,000 of capital the Universal Credit upper-limit boundary is applied differently: UKMOD uses a strict > 16,000 limit and still pays a tariff-reduced award (251.30/month for a single owner-occupier at 16,000), while the composed rulespec-uk pipeline ends entitlement at capital >= 16,000 (regulation 18 encoded as a >= gate) and returns nil. Only the exact-threshold case differs; capital of 6,000, 6,250 and 10,000 match on both sides and 20,000 is nil on both.

workaround.description: Classify the exact-16,000 boundary as a reconciled convention difference in dispositions/uk-universal-credit.yaml; the tariff-reduced UKMOD award at the threshold reconciles to the single standard allowance less the tariff income on capital above the 6,000 floor.

entries.summary: In UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03 (system UK_2026), when a taxpayer has both taxable savings income (yiytx) and taxable dividend income (ydvtx), the model grants the savings income a 0% band equal to the dividend income amount, zeroing income tax that the Income Tax Act 2007 sections 11D/12/12A charge on that savings at the savings basic, higher, or additional rate. tin_s for a savings-plus-dividend taxpayer therefore falls short of the statutory liability by (min(savings above the personal savings allowance, dividend income)) times the marginal savings rate. Savings-only and dividend-only cases are unaffected and match the source-grounded RuleSpec to the penny.

statutory_evidence.rule: Savings income above the starting-rate band and the personal savings allowance is charged at the savings basic/higher/additional rate (ITA 2007 s.11D), independently of any dividend income; the starting rate for savings (s.12) is reduced only by non-savings income, not by dividend income.

workaround.description: Restrict the exact-match UKMOD savings/dividend income-tax oracle to savings-only (uk-income-tax-savings) and dividend-only (uk-income-tax-dividend) cases, which UKMOD computes correctly. Keep the mixed savings-and-dividend cases (uk-income-tax-mixed) in the grid with dispositions (dispositions/uk-income-tax-mixed.yaml) that reconcile each residual as this upstream engine gap; do not weaken the source-grounded RuleSpec savings-tax computation to match UKMOD.

entries.summary: UKMOD's Child Benefit output bch_s does NOT embed the benefit take-up correction that means-tested benefits carry. The take-up draw i_rand_tu (seeded by the DEF policies BTA_uk and random_uk) gates only the means-tested policies (bsauc_uk Universal Credit, bho_uk Housing Benefit, bsa_uk Income Support, bwkmt_bfamt_uk tax credits, bmu_uk Council Tax Benefit); the Child Benefit policy bch_uk (a non-means-tested BenCalc on the first-child and other-child rates) has no i_rand_tu gate, consistent with Child Benefit being a near-universal UK entitlement. Verified live on UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03 UK_2026: for one/two/three children at 20k/70k/80k/90k earnings, bch_s (net of the bchrd_s High Income Child Benefit Charge clawback) plus bchrd_s is invariant to income at 1410.46/2343.82/3277.18 per year, and toggling the take-up policy switch overrides (BTA_uk and random_uk off) leaves bch_s and bchrd_s unchanged in every case. The take-up hazard the household Universal Credit suite documents (ukmod-uc-bsauc-takeup-correction) therefore does not affect the Child Benefit comparison.

attempted_switches.BTA_uk_off: No effect on bch_s or bchrd_s (as expected: bch_uk has no take-up gate). Requested on every uk-child-benefit case for explicitness and parity with the household Universal Credit suite.
attempted_switches.random_uk_off: No effect on bch_s or bchrd_s for the same reason.

workaround.description: None needed for take-up. The uk-child-benefit suite compares the composed rulespec-uk gross s.141 entitlement against UKMOD's pre-charge Child Benefit, reconstructed by summing the euromod target list [bch_s, bchrd_s] (bch_s is net of the bchrd_uk High Income Child Benefit Charge clawback; adding bchrd_s back recovers the gross amount). The High Income Child Benefit Charge is not encoded on the Axiom side (its ITEPA 2003 s.681B-H provisions are not in the corpus, rulespec-uk#75), so the comparison is gross-to-gross. The only residual is the UKMOD 52.14-week vs Axiom 52-week annualisation convention (~0.27%), absorbed by the concept's 0.3% relative tolerance; all 12 cases match.

entries.summary: UKMOD's Pension Credit output boamt_s (guarantee credit boamtmm_s + savings credit boamtxp_s, computed inside the bsa_uk social-assistance policy) embeds a take-up and Universal-Credit-transition correction: the take-up estimates $PCGCSCTU = 0.69 (guarantee, or guarantee+savings) and $PCSCTU = 0.37 (savings only) drive an i_rand_tu draw and an i_bsa_noUC / i_bsa_yesUC transition split, so for a hypothetical benefit unit some units are marked as transitioned to Universal Credit and return a zero Pension Credit award that is not the statutory entitlement. This draw is STOCHASTIC per row, NOT deterministic per composition. Corrected 2026-07-05 (batch-size-1 integrity audit): the earlier claim of a deterministic paid/zero pattern (e.g. single at 2000/year state pension pays 867.50 while 0/6000/8000 zero) was WRONG — those were one non-reproducible realization from running the whole pensioner grid in a single batch. Verified live on UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03 (system UK_2026, dataset training_data): (a) at --comparison-batch-size 1 every Pension Credit case, including a single pensioner with zero income who is unambiguously entitled to the full 238.00/week guarantee credit, returns boamt_s = 0.0 (identical with the take-up policy switches off, none, or on) — an isolated household always draws non-take, so batch size 1 is degenerate for this instrument; (b) running ten byte-for-byte identical copies of the entitled single-income0 household in one run returns [0.0, 238.00, 0.0, 0.0, 238.00, 0.0, 0.0, 238.00, 238.00, 238.00] — identical facts, different awards purely by position; (c) the whole-suite mismatch count is itself batch-size dependent (9 at batch size 1, 5 at 2, 6 at 3/4/6, 4 all-in-one-batch) with no monotone or composition-based pattern. Where a unit does take up, the paid boamt_s equals the Axiom guarantee-credit entitlement exactly (single standard minimum guarantee 238.00/week, couple 363.25/week, less the assessed state pension), so the Axiom encoding is correct and the zeros are a UKMOD-side stochastic artefact.

attempted_switches.random_uk_off: No effect on the zeroing: setting random_uk off leaves the take-up / UC-transition draw active inside bsa_uk (verified: results identical with random_uk on and off). This does NOT establish deterministic take-up behaviour — it only shows the exposed switch does not disable the i_rand_tu draw.
attempted_switches.BTA_uk_off: No effect for the same reason.
attempted_switches.per_case_isolation: Batch size 1 is degenerate here (corrected 2026-07-05): an isolated Pension Credit household always draws non-take, so every case returns 0.0 at --comparison-batch-size 1. Unlike a pure batch-position contamination, batch size 1 does not recover the entitlement for this instrument; the only per-household-deterministic configuration would force 100% take-up (disable the i_rand_tu gate). Update (per-household adapter isolation, 2026-07-06): the worker now runs every household as its own engine run, so each case reproducibly gets its solo draw sequence — WHICH cases zero is now stable across runs, batch sizes, and batch compositions (no more realization-by-batch). This stabilises the recorded realization; it does not recover the statutory entitlement for cases whose solo draw marks non-take. Forcing 100% take-up now has a working mechanism: the adapter's euromod_constant_overrides patches DefConst values (e.g. the take-up rates) into the system XML on the model overlay — the connector's constantsToOverwrite kwarg silently ignores DefConst constants. Adopting it for this suite is a deliberate regeneration (values flip from take-up realizations to statutory entitlements), tracked for the suite owner.

workaround.description: Compare the composed rulespec-uk Pension Credit guarantee-credit award against the executed boamt_s and classify take-up / UC-transition zeroing as a UKMOD-side stochastic artefact, not an Axiom encoding mismatch. Because the draw is not reproducible per household, the committed dashboard report is one realization: it records the take-up zeros produced by running the whole pensioner grid in a single batch, dispositioned by pinned value. UKMOD reports boamt_s monthly; the adapter divides it by UKMOD's weekly-to-monthly factor (365/7/12) so the comparison is weekly-to-weekly against the pipeline's weekly award. Where a unit takes up, the paid boamt_s matches the guarantee-credit entitlement exactly (single standard minimum guarantee 238.00/week = 1034.17/month, couple 363.25/week = 1578.41/month, less the assessed state pension); the take-up-zeroed points are dispositioned rather than absorbed by tolerance. A future adapter fix that forces 100% take-up would make this suite deterministic; batch size 1 alone makes it degenerate (all zero) and is not a fix.
workaround.assessable_income: UKMOD's Pension Credit income test assesses the state pension boact_s (uprated from the boact00 state-pension data input), not a poa private pension; the suite supplies assessable income through boact00 and bridges the assessed boact_s into the pipeline so both engines test the identical income.

entries.summary: UKMOD simulates Pension Credit savings credit (output boamtxp_s, with UK_2026 constants $PCSCThreshSing = 208.07#w, $PCSCMaxSing = 17.96#w, savings-credit withdrawal rate $PCSCwr = 0.40, and an eligibility condition dag >= 65 with qualifying income above the savings-credit threshold), but on the registration-free demo data boamtxp_s returns nil across the groundable pensioner income range. Verified live on UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03 (system UK_2026): a single claimant aged 70 (a pre-6-April-2016 pension-age reacher) with state pension swept from 10,000 to 14,000/year in 200 steps returns boamtxp_s = 0 at every point, because the guarantee credit already tops assessable income to the minimum and the savings-credit population is closed to pre-6-April-2016 reachers. The compared total boamt_s therefore equals its guarantee-credit component boamtmm_s on this data.

workaround.description: Scope the composed rulespec-uk pipeline comparison to the guarantee credit (the exercisable regime) and compare against boamt_s, which equals boamtmm_s on the demo data. Savings credit is separately encoded in rulespec-uk (uk/statutes/ukpga/2002/16/3) and remains available for a data configuration that exercises it; its nil value here is a demo-data exercisability limit, not an Axiom encoding gap. The severe-disability and carer additional amounts (encoded in the pipeline from regulation 6(5)/(8)) are similarly not exercised because UKMOD applies the severe-disability premium only when a disability benefit is present in the data (bdisc/bdimb/... > 0), which the hypothetical rows do not carry.

entries.summary: UKMOD's Housing Benefit output bho_s is deterministically zeroed for a WORKING-AGE benefit unit by the Universal-Credit transition inside bho_uk (the i_bho_noUC / i_bho_yesUC split). The bho_uk model comment states the intent verbatim: 'ensure new benefit claims are to UC only and not to the legacy benefits'. A hypothetical working-age renter is treated as a new claim, routed to Universal Credit, and its legacy bho_s is forced to zero — UKMOD would instead pay the Universal Credit housing element (compared separately in the uk-universal-credit suite). This is NOT the stochastic take-up draw that zeros the Universal Credit and Pension Credit awards: it is deterministic. Verified live on UKMOD_PUBLIC_B2026.03 (system UK_2026, dataset training_data): every working-age renter with a positive statutory Housing Benefit entitlement returns bho_s = 0.0, and the zeroed set is IDENTICAL across repeated runs (single under-25 renter, single renter, and couple renter all return 0.0 on both of two consecutive full-suite runs), unlike i_rand_tu which varies by row position. Pinning the three HB take-up rates $HBTUWAWork / $HBTUWANowork / $HBTUPen to 1.0 via euromod_constant_overrides does not restore a working-age award, confirming the take-up draw is not the cause. Pension-age Housing Benefit is not subject to the transition (it remains a live legacy benefit): the single and couple pension-age no-earnings cases pay bho_s and match the composed rulespec-uk Housing Benefit entitlement to the penny. So the Axiom encoding is correct (it computes the full statutory Housing Benefit entitlement the HB Regulations 2006 confer) and the working-age zeros are a UKMOD-side current-law caseload-routing behaviour, not an Axiom encoding gap.

attempted_switches.BTA_uk_off: No effect: the adapter policy-switch override sets BTA_uk off, but the working-age zero is the UC transition (i_bho_noUC / i_bho_yesUC), not the take-up draw, so the award still zeros.
attempted_switches.random_uk_off: No effect for the same reason (the suite runs with random_uk off and the working-age zeros persist deterministically).
attempted_switches.HB_takeup_rates_pinned_to_1: No effect on the working-age zero: euromod_constant_overrides pins $HBTUWAWork / $HBTUWANowork / $HBTUPen to 1.0, which forces 100% take-up, yet the working-age award stays zero — isolating the cause to the UC transition rather than take-up.
attempted_switches.UCtransition_zero: Setting $UCtransition=0 does not restore a working-age legacy award either (bho_s stays 0.0) and perturbs UKMOD's assessed HB means ymn01_s that the suite bridges into both engines, so it is not used; the working-age closure is structural for UK_2026.

workaround.description: Compare the composed rulespec-uk Housing Benefit entitlement against the executed bho_s and grade the parity on the PENSION-AGE population, where UKMOD Housing Benefit stays live and both engines pay it (single and couple pension-age no-earnings renters match to the penny — the maximum-benefit path). The three working-age renter cases, which UKMOD deterministically zeros via the UC transition, are dispositioned upstream_engine_gap in dispositions/uk-housing-benefit.yaml with the full statutory entitlement pinned as the Axiom value (single under-25 6000.00, single 6600.00, couple 7800.00). The disposition is stable because the zero is deterministic, unlike the Pension Credit and Universal Credit take-up zeros whose realization is a stochastic draw.

entries.summary: The Danish child and youth benefit taper policy bfachnm_dk retains a pre-2022 spousal income test in DK_2022 through DK_2025: for cohabiting and married recipients the boerne- og ungeydelsesloven § 1 a reduction is driven off a partner/couple income basis rather than the post-2022 individualized taper (each recipient tapered on their own mellemskat basis after § 4, stk. 1 ligedeling). The dk-child-youth-benefit-couple witness now activates the divergence: for a married couple with one age-5 child, one recipient earning 1500000 kr. and the other earning zero, EUROMOD DK_2025 executes a 7504 kr. household benefit while the current-law Axiom household sum is 8384 kr. (earner 0 plus non-earner 8384). Single-recipient households remain unaffected because there is no partner income to test.

workaround.description: Keep the original dk-child-youth-benefit grid single-parent so its seven baseline cases retain raw parity, and disposition the explicit married single-earner dk-child-youth-benefit-couple witness as an upstream_engine_gap linked to ec-jrc issue #18. The Axiom couple pipeline executes each § 4, stk. 1 recipient separately, tapers only that recipient's own § 1 a basis, and sums the two values to the same household level as EUROMOD bfachnm_s.

entries.summary: For 2023 the boerne- og ungeydelsesloven § 1, stk. 3 adds a one-off uplift of 660 kr. 'samlet' (combined) across the stk. 1-2 amounts. EUROMOD DK_2023 applies a 600 kr. supplement instead of the statutory 660 kr., so the DK_2023 bfachnm_s exceeds the un-supplemented amount by 600 rather than 660 (observed: a single-parent age-5 case at 300000 income returns 15624 annual, 600 above the 15024 base rather than 660). DK_2025 does not apply the 2023 supplement, so this suite's DK_2025 grid is unaffected.

workaround.description: Run the dedicated dk-child-youth-benefit-2023 witness with the statutory 660 kr. increase supplied to Axiom and disposition EUROMOD's executed 15624-vs-15684 mismatch as an upstream_engine_gap linked to ec-jrc issue #19. The main DK_2025 lane remains unaffected because the one-off increase applies only in 2023.

entries.summary: The boerne- og ungeydelsesloven § 1 a, stk. 4-5 reduces the taper income basis by the recipient's qualifying retirement contributions (aldersforsikring, aldersopsparing and supplerende engangssum per pensionsbeskatningslovens §§ 10 A, 12 A and 29 A), capped at the § 16, stk. 1 grundbeloeb and grossed up by dividing by 0,6. EUROMOD's bfachnm_dk taper does not apply this pension deduction/gross-up, so it tapers on the un-reduced mellemskat basis. The dk-child-youth-benefit suite now activates the divergence with a 60000 kr. contribution witness: at tintbto 1196000 and the 917000 threshold, with the ORDINARY 2025 PBL § 16 cap of 9400 kr. that applies to the age-35 recipient (the higher 61200 kr. cap holds only from the seventh income year before folkepensionsalderen), Axiom subtracts the 15666.67 gross-up and pays 11497.33 while EUROMOD pays 11184 — a 313.33 kr. gap, 2 pct. of the missing gross-up.

workaround.description: Keep the original seven dk-child-youth-benefit cases at zero qualifying retirement contributions so they retain raw parity, and disposition the explicit 60000 kr. contribution witness as an upstream_engine_gap linked to ec-jrc issue #20. The Axiom side applies the § 1 a, stk. 4-5 cap and gross-up; EUROMOD has no bfachnm_dk taper input for it.
